title: The trustworthy
hookLine: before prophethood, Muhammad was a merchant known as al-Amin, the trustworthy (Ibn Ishaq, Life of the Prophet)
last: A HOUSEHOLDER'S LIFE, LIVED WITH GOD IN MIND.

lines: SHE HAS HEARD OF ONE MAN.
cards: Khadijah has a problem. She's a merchant woman of Mecca with goods to send to Syria, and she needs someone to take them, sell them, and bring the profit back. That's a lot of trust to hand someone on a long road.
The early biography of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, written by Ibn Ishaq, says she had heard of one man's truthfulness, his trustworthiness and his good character.
Long before anyone called him a prophet, the people of his town had a name for him.

teach.b: Al-Amin. The trustworthy. First, where it comes from.

Ibn Ishaq says that among his people, the Quraysh, Muhammad was called al-Amin. Not for a miracle, not for a sermon, but for how he handled other people's things and other people's words. Second, the deal.
Khadijah offered him her goods to trade in Syria, and sent her servant Maysara along.
Ibn Ishaq says Muhammad sold what he had brought, bought what he wanted, and came home, and that Khadijah was impressed by what she heard. In time she proposed marriage, and they married.
Muslims remember her with deep love, and tradition says she was the first to believe in his message. Third, the name in use.
The tribes of Mecca were rebuilding the Kaaba and quarreled over who would set the Black Stone back in its place. Ibn Ishaq says they agreed to let the next man through the gate decide.
It was Muhammad, and they said, in effect, here is al-Amin, we're satisfied.
He spread out a cloak, laid the stone on it, had a leader from each clan lift a corner, then set it in place himself. Fourth, why Muslims hold this up.
The Qur'an tells believers to return what's entrusted to them to its owners.
A saying of the Prophet, in the collection of al-Tirmidhi, puts the honest, trustworthy merchant in the company of the prophets and the truthful.

teach.h: A FAIR SCALE IS PART OF FAITH.
teach.b: In these teachings, trade is not outside faith.
A fair scale and a kept promise are part of it.

how: Muslims remember the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as al-Amin and hold up honest trade, fair weights and kept trusts as part of faith, drawing on the Qur'an and hadith.

o: al-Amin, Mecca's name for Muhammad as a merchant
the name of Khadijah's servant on the trip
a title for a judge appointed by a caliph

games.q: al-Amin in Ibn Ishaq — tap the pairs.
p: sent her goods to Syria with him
lifted on a cloak by every clan

s: Muhammad was first called al-Amin after he became a prophet
Ibn Ishaq says his people called him that before prophethood.
Khadijah hired him because she had heard of his honesty
Ibn Ishaq says she had heard of his truthfulness, trustworthiness and good character.
in Islam, trade is kept separate from faith
a saying in al-Tirmidhi puts the honest, trustworthy merchant in the company of the prophets.

games.q: the clans of Mecca are quarreling over who gets the honor of setting the Black Stone back in the Kaaba. the next man through the gate is asked to decide. you're him. what do you do?
o: choose the strongest clan, to keep the peace.
spread a cloak, put the stone on it, and let each clan lift a corner.
set it in place yourself and say nothing.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says Muhammad, called al-Amin, laid the stone on a cloak, had each clan's leader lift a corner, then set it in place himself. everyone shared the honor.

practice: Think of the small deals in your week, not only money: a promise to call back, a borrowed charger, a favor you said you'd do.
Let one come up where you've been a little loose, a detail left out, a promise half kept, and without judging, picture making it completely clean: the full truth, the thing returned, the word kept.
If you pray, you can bring it to God in your own tradition's words.

wordCard.voice: The trustworthy. Al-Amin: what the people of Mecca called the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, as a merchant, before prophethood. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, from the Islamic tradition: the trustworthy, the name the Prophet ﷺ was known by in Mecca.

carryVoice: Your line: trustworthy. A name his town gave him long before any sermon. Until tomorrow.
